wiktionary.gloss: A new growth of or on a plant, whether from seed or other parts.

examples: Near-synonyms: seedling, chit
wiktionary.gloss: A germinated seed, an incipient young plant.
An edible variety of such, grown and intended as food; examples include bean, alfalfa, kale, and others.
A bean sprout.

examples: Oh my, how your sprouts have grown!
wiktionary.gloss: A child.

examples: In our family we only eat sprouts once a year, at Christmas.
wiktionary.gloss: A Brussels sprout.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English sprouten, spruten, from Old English sprūtan, from Proto-West Germanic *spreutan, from Proto-Germanic *spreutaną.

senses.definition: To start to produce leaves, buds, or shoots, or to begin growing.

examples.en: The beans are sprouting faster than expected.
examples.vi: Hạt đậu đang nảy mầm nhanh hơn dự kiến.

examples.en: He noticed several grey hairs sprouting on his beard.
examples.vi: Anh ấy nhận thấy vài sợi râu trắng mọc lên ở cằm.

senses.definition: To appear or develop quickly and in large numbers.

examples.en: Trendy cafes have sprouted up all over the neighborhood.
examples.vi: Những quán cà phê thời thượng đã mọc lên khắp khu phố.

thesaurus.definition: produce buds, branches, or germinate
put forth and grow sprouts or shoots

examples: The crocuses should be sprouting after 2 months, provided they're well tended.
wiktionary.gloss: To grow from seed; to germinate.

examples: I sprouted beans and radishes and put them in my salad.
wiktionary.gloss: To cause to grow from a seed.

examples: to sprout potatoes
wiktionary.gloss: To deprive of sprouts.
To emerge from the ground as sprouts.

examples: Whiskers sprouted from the old man's chin.
wiktionary.gloss: To emerge haphazardly from a surface.

examples: A lot of coffee shops have sprouted up in this neighbourhood since the block of flats was put up.
wiktionary.gloss: To emerge or appear haphazardly.

thesaurus.definition: take apart into its constituent pieces
divide into pieces
make a mathematical, chemical, or grammatical analysis of; break down into components or essential features

examples: I carefully took the clock mechanism apart to clean it.
wiktionary.gloss: To dismantle something into its component pieces.
To soundly defeat someone, or a (sport) team.
to criticise someone

vi_block: Sự náo loạn, sự rối loạn; sự ẩu đả.

examples: Why does all this fluff accumulate in the turn-ups?
wiktionary.gloss: Fabric turned up at the bottom of trousers to make them shorter.
A fight or disturbance.

examples: I'll bet $10 that the next turn-up is an ace.
wiktionary.gloss: The next card taken from the top of a pack of cards and displayed.
A stroke of good luck; something that appears unexpectedly; especially in turn up for the book.
A book, intended for children, with flaps that can be lifted to reveal underlying text or images.

thesaurus.definition: a transmission from Earth to a spacecraft or the path of such a transmission

wiktionary.gloss: The portion of a communications link used for the transmission of signals from a ground station to a satellite or to an airborne platform.
The communication path from a mobile device to a base station, a consumer to the network backbone, a client device to a server, etc.
Data transmission from a data station to the headend.
To transmit a signal by means of an uplink.
An informal greeting.
An expression of concern, asking for an explanation.

blocks.etymology: Popularized by the teen comedy Heathers (1989).

examples: What's your damage?
wiktionary.gloss: What is wrong with X? What's X's problem? Is X crazy?
The state or condition of being operational or of functioning acceptably.
